text: Lesson 20 read a file manually, line by line. Here's what that actually looks like in real, professional practice — one line.
Read CSV opens the file, parses every row, infers every column's type, and hands you back a ready-to-use DataFrame. Everything Lesson 20 built by hand, done properly, in a single call.
Read JSON works the same way, when the JSON file is shaped as a list of objects — exactly Lesson 15's list of dictionaries. Lesson 24 goes deeper into JSON shapes that aren't quite this simple.

Two parameters matter constantly. Parse dates converts a column to a real date and time type instead of loading it as plain text — without it, you can't filter by year or month directly. D-type overrides Pandas's automatic guess for one column — keeping something like vendor I-D as text, even though it looks numeric, exactly like Lesson 14 warned about.
Get the type right at read time, and you avoid debugging it three lessons later. Next lesson: REST APIs — getting data that has no file to read at all. See you there.
